newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia coffee fund notches 100 bln peso surplus.
newsitem.headline: Colombia coffee fund notches 100 bln peso surplus.

text.p: Colombia's National Coffee Fund notched up a 100 billion peso (about US$91 million) surplus in first half 1997 compared to a 200 billion peso deficit in the same period last year.

Jorge Cardenas, head of National Coffee Growers' Federation which administers the fund under contract with the government, said Colombia earned $400 million from coffee exports from Jan 30 to June 30.
Total earnings in the 1996/97 coffee year to the end of June are about $1.7 billion, he said.
The federation uses export earnings to pay Colombian growers a guaranteed price for their coffee and after deducting costs invests the profits in the fund.
The fund is used to finance a range of activities from coffee marketing campaign to agricultural research and key infrastructure projects in the main coffee -growing regions.

Cardenas forecast the fund would post a surplus of about 300 billion pesos by the end of the year thanks to sharp rises in international bean prices -- giving added stability to the coffee industry in Colombia.
Last December, in the face of low prices and soaring production costs, Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo predicted the coffee fund would be more than $465 million in the red by this September.
